rule_or_pattern: Gender markers are misread systematically: '(6)' / '(5)' → '(ὁ)'; '(ή)' → '(ἡ)'; '(το)' → '(τὸ)'; the feminine abbreviation 'θ.' read as '6.' or '0.' after a French word: regex (?<=[a-zé\-], )[60]\.(?=\s|$|,) → 'θ.' (also inside 'portion, 6.' etc.). If relabelling is not applied, drop lines containing '(6)', '(5)', '(ή)', '(το)' or ', 6.' / ', 0.'. Gutter-crossing lines (21-40 type) go by the pool rule.
notes: 1878 Greek-French dictionary (Varvatis), two columns, dev split. Running French and Greek text reads correctly (1, 3, 7, 10, 15, 18-20), but the grammatical markers are misread consistently: the article '(ὁ)' becomes '(6)'/'(5)' (25, 36, 37), '(ἡ)'/'(τὸ)' lose breathing/accent as '(ή)'/'(το)' (4, 11, 12, 13), and the feminine marker 'θ.' becomes '6.' or '0.' (11, 16, 17); the '‖ —' sign is read as 'Η' (8). Lines 21-40 are gutter-crossing merges (about 5% of the book) and should be dropped.
